questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: How the Pirenne thesis works
questions.learningObjective: Identify the break that the Pirenne thesis relocates
questions.stem: Ticket 1201 asks whether the Pirenne thesis moves the real break to the Arab conquests rather than the Germanic invasions.

options.text: It argues Mediterranean trade and culture survived until the Arab conquests closed that sea.
It argues Germanic kings ended Roman unity in the fifth century.
options.misconception: treats the Germanic invasions as the real break

options.text: It argues the Reformation created a new European order in the sixteenth century.
options.misconception: confuses the thesis with Reformation periodisation

options.text: It argues the French Revolution ended the ancient world in 1789.
options.misconception: projects a modern political break onto antiquity

questions.explanation: The Pirenne thesis relocates the break to the Arab conquests because Mediterranean unity, in its view, survived the Germanic invasions. The tempting error is to treat the fifth-century invasions as the end of antiquity.
questions.hint: Trace where the thesis puts the break.

questions.topic: What the phrase modern period does
